# Local arrests {#local-arrests}

Some of the most common stories in local news outlets examine the growth of arrests by ICE and the failure of the federal government to focus mainly on convicted criminals. Across the country, reporters have found that few of the people arrested have violent convictions, and less than half have any criminal history at all.

We have enhanced the original data to include some more information on the person's most serious criminal conviction and the first place they were detained after the arrest.

You can use the same approach for each of the following story recipes to get a dataset that contains  your state or local area.

## Get your local data

It's more difficult than it should be to get the arrest data for your area. One solution is to stick with analysis at the state level since July 2025.

There are several alternatives:

1. In very populated areas, use the EOR Area of Responsibility. This is the ICE office in charge of your area and differentiates between, for example, Northern and Southern California. But it combines many states in the interior of the country. You can look up your state on the ICE website to find the areas of responsibility, searching for your state "Enforcement and Removal Operations":

![ICE ERO office example](/assets/images/erosearch-page.png)

2. Use all of the data for your state. We expect most people will do this. Since July 2025, this is pretty reliable. Before then, about 10 percent of the rows were missing the state. This means that any trends will OVERSTATE the increase in arrests, since there are likely some arrests from earlier periods that should have been marked as in  your state but weren't. You can supplement this with information from detention and detainer sites where the state is missing.  We have found that XX percent of the missing information could be filled in using those tables, but there are still YY with missing states.

3. Use the closest place of first detention instead of all arrests. This, too, will overstate the increase in arrests between the Biden and Trump years, because fewer people were automatically detained before 2025. But it will provide you with more local data for the past year.
